grade_label: Partially implemented / steps taken, further action needed
text: Consider establishing a national mechanism to identify and protect child victims of trafficking to ensure that child victims are not treated as offenders
rationale: Denmark adopted a National Action Plan to Combat Trafficking in Human Beings 2022-2025 (with a 2026-2029 plan in preparation) and established a Special Crime Unit; CAT, CEDAW and the DIHR report a persistently low number of investigations and convictions, a limited recovery and reflection period, and no independent national rapporteur.
sources: A/HRC/WG.6/52/DNK/2 para. 30; A/HRC/WG.6/52/DNK/1 para. 73; A/HRC/WG.6/52/DNK/3 para. 8
evidence_quotes:
UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/52/DNK/2), para. 30 — Committee against Torture: "welcomed the adoption by Denmark of a National Action Plan to Combat Trafficking in Human Beings 2022-2025. However, it was concerned about the low number of investigations and convictions for trafficking in human beings and the limited recovery and reflection period for victims"
National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/52/DNK/1), para. 73 — Denmark: "A new action plan against human trafficking for the period of 2026-2029 is under preparation"
Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/52/DNK/3), para. 8 — Danish Institute for Human Rights: "a low number of convictions for trafficking of human beings, while the number of persons exposed to trafficking had increased ... establish a permanent, independent National Rapporteur"

primary_theme: Labour rights and right to work

action_summary: Anti-discrimination framework; national action plan against racism
grade_label: Partially implemented / steps taken, further action needed
text: Develop comprehensive anti-discrimination legislation that prohibits differential treatment based on all grounds of discrimination
rationale: Denmark has a broad anti-discrimination legal framework and in February 2025 adopted a National Action Plan against Racism with 36 initiatives, alongside successive action plans against antisemitism; CERD and stakeholders nonetheless report persistent gaps - no legislative prohibition of racial or ethnic profiling, weak hate-crime data, and a 2025 plan criticised for limited scope and for lacking a definition of racism.

evidence_quotes:

UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/52/DNK/2), para. 9 — Committee on the Elimination of Racial Discrimination: "expressed concern about the lack of a clear prohibition of racial profiling and of operational guidelines to combat racial profiling"

action_summary: Protect LGBTI persons from discrimination
grade_label: Partially implemented / steps taken, further action needed
text: Adopt comprehensive anti-discrimination legislation in Greenland that encompasses all the prohibited grounds of discrimination, including sexual orientation and gender identity
rationale: Denmark strengthened protection of LGBT+ people in December 2021 by adding gender identity, gender expression and sex characteristics to the hate-crime, hate-speech and discrimination laws, funds LGBT+ action plans and introduced 'co-fatherhood' in 2025; legal gender recognition for minors regardless of age was rejected by Parliament in January 2025.
sources: A/HRC/WG.6/52/DNK/1 para. 29; A/HRC/WG.6/52/DNK/3 para. 50
evidence_quotes:
National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/52/DNK/1), para. 29 — Denmark: "In December 2021, Denmark strengthened the protection of LGBT+ people by explicitly referring to gender identity, gender expression and sex characteristics as grounds of protection in the Danish laws covering hate crimes, hate speech and discrimination"
Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/52/DNK/3), para. 50 — Joint submission 2: "legal gender recognition regardless of age had not been adopted, following the rejection of a parliamentary proposal in January 2025"

action_summary: Prevent and address sexual and gender-based violence
grade_label: Partially implemented / steps taken, further action needed
text: Continue the development of programmes to combat the sexual abuse of children in Greenland
rationale: Denmark adopted a consent-based rape law (2020), a National Action Plan on Intimate Partner Violence and Killings 2023-2026, psychological-violence provisions, a victims' hotline and new shelters (including for men, 2024); CEDAW, CAT and JS2 report rising gender-based violence, few rape convictions, and the Istanbul Convention still not applied to Greenland and the Faroe Islands.
sources: A/HRC/WG.6/52/DNK/2 para. 35; A/HRC/WG.6/52/DNK/2 para. 36; A/HRC/WG.6/52/DNK/3 para. 46
evidence_quotes:
UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/52/DNK/2), para. 35 — Committee against Torture: "welcomed the adoption of the National Action Plan to Combat Intimate Partner Violence and Intimate Partner Killings 2023-2026"
UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/52/DNK/2), para. 36 — Committee on the Elimination of Discrimination against Women: "it noted with concern the rise in gender-based violence against women, high incidences of sexual violence against women with disabilities and the reported high prevalence of sexual harassment in the workplace and the education system"
Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/52/DNK/3), para. 46 — Joint submission 2: "a small proportion of reported cases of rape resulting in convictions, and a high number of suspected femicides in the first half of 2025"

action_summary: Anti-discrimination framework; national action plan against racism
grade_label: Partially implemented / steps taken, further action needed
text: Introduce legislation to protect residents of Greenland against discrimination on all recognized grounds, within and outside the labour market, including establishing an independent appeals board
rationale: Denmark has a broad anti-discrimination legal framework and in February 2025 adopted a National Action Plan against Racism with 36 initiatives, alongside successive action plans against antisemitism; CERD and stakeholders nonetheless report persistent gaps - no legislative prohibition of racial or ethnic profiling, weak hate-crime data, and a 2025 plan criticised for limited scope and for lacking a definition of racism.
sources: A/HRC/WG.6/52/DNK/1 para. 112; A/HRC/WG.6/52/DNK/3 para. 21; A/HRC/WG.6/52/DNK/2 para. 9
evidence_quotes:
National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/52/DNK/1), para. 112 — Denmark: "In February 2025, the Danish Government presented a national action plan against racism with 36 initiatives and the ambition to fight racism in a variety of areas in society"
Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/52/DNK/3), para. 21 — Joint submission 1; Joint submission 2: "welcomed the adoption of a national action plan against racism in February 2025. However, they were concerned that the plan had limitations in scope and lacked a clear definition of racism"
UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/52/DNK/2), para. 9 — Committee on the Elimination of Racial Discrimination: "expressed concern about the lack of a clear prohibition of racial profiling and of operational guidelines to combat racial profiling"

action_summary: Strengthen the national human rights institution
grade_label: Partially implemented / steps taken, further action needed
text: Consider establishing a human rights institution for the Faroe Islands in accordance with the principles relating to the status of national institutions for the promotion and protection of human rights
rationale: The Danish Institute for Human Rights retains A-status accreditation; the Human Rights Committee has asked Denmark to amend the DIHR Act to secure an independent board-removal procedure, liability protection and adequate funding, and no NHRI has yet been established in the Faroe Islands.
sources: A/HRC/WG.6/52/DNK/2 para. 4; A/HRC/WG.6/52/DNK/1 para. 150
evidence_quotes:
UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/52/DNK/2), para. 4 — Human Rights Committee: "amending the Act on the Danish Institute for Human Rights to establish an independent procedure for removal of board members ... guaranteeing adequate funding to fulfil its mandate"
National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/52/DNK/1), para. 150 — Denmark: "The Government has explored different options for establishing a national human rights institution [in the Faroe Islands], adapted to the small Faroese society, and will continue to do so"
